First beacon home. The Lanternfish's lamps catch something below: a pulse, steady as a heartbeat.
Two lights recovered. Ines logs the pulse: it repeats every forty seconds, from deeper than our charts go.
Kito swears the pulse changed pitch when we surfaced the last beacon. Bram says it's the hull creaking.
The old survey map ends here. Past this ridge the seabed is just a blank page marked 'unsounded'.
We dropped a marker buoy on the ridge. Whatever sends that pulse, we'll find our way back to it.
A dead research probe drifts past, its lamp still blinking. Its last log mentions the same pulse.
Odile cracked the probe's memory: three more beacons were lost along this trench. We'll recover them.
The pulse is clearer now. Ines thinks it is not a signal at all, but an answer.
Strange lights in the dark: a field of glowing jellies parts around our hull and closes behind us.
Ten dives logged. The crew is fast now; nobody wastes a signal. The trench mouth opens below.
Cold water floods the outer lockers. Bram fixes it with tape and stubbornness. We dive on.
The beacons down here are older, crusted with coral. Someone placed them long before us.
A second pulse joins the first, out of step. Kito calls it a duet. Ines calls it a warning.
Sonar paints a wall ahead, a ridge of black stone carved too straight to be natural.
We found a gate in the wall, shut tight. Something large circles on the other side.
The Warden of the Trench blocks the gate. Every sonar ping we send comes back louder.
Past the Warden, the water is warm. Act two: the hidden basin, and whatever built that gate.
Bioluminescent reefs line the basin floor like city streets. The pulse leads straight down them.
We recovered a beacon shaped like a shell. Odile hums along with its tone without noticing.
The basin has currents that run in circles. Twice we nearly lost the drone. Twice we got it back.
Ines found carvings near a beacon: the same task marks we use, one to five, in someone else's hand.
Our lamps flicker every time the pulse peaks. Bram reroutes power. Nobody likes the silence after.
The relay buoy is jammed. For a while we dive with no word from the surface. We trust each other.
Halfway through the basin. Kito marks the map: twenty-three beacons home, none lost on the way.
A swarm of tiny lights follows the Lanternfish, copying our signals back to us, a beat late.
The swarm learns fast. It mimics our pings well enough to fool the drone. Signals must be sure now.
Odile names the swarm 'the Choir'. Ines asks her not to name things that might want to eat us.
Below the reefs, a dead zone: our sonar shows nothing at all. We dive by memory and order marks.
We came out of the dead zone with every task done. Bram says that's the best crew he's served with.
The Choir has gathered at a narrow pass, thousands strong, humming the pulse back at the deep.
Ines thinks the Choir guards the way down. Kito thinks it is waiting to see if we are worthy.
One more beacon before the pass. The pulse is so strong now we feel it in our teeth.
The Gatekeeper Swarm closes the pass. Every card must land exactly; one mistake and it swallows the light.
The Swarm parted. Act three: the abyss, where the pulse begins.
No reefs here, no swarm, only black water and the slow climb of the depth gauge.
A beacon older than any we've found, its tone low and patient. Ines records it twice to be sure.
Pressure alarms sing for an hour. Bram keeps them company with bad jokes. We hold together.
The pulse slows down when we work as one crew. Kito noticed first. Now we all feel it.
We pass a field of wrecked submarines, none of them ours, none of them human-made.
Odile reads the wrecks: each one turned back at the same depth. We keep going.
Silence again: no signals allowed in this stretch of the abyss. We plan with our eyes.
The drone's lamp died for a minute. When it came back it was glowing the pulse's colour.
Forty-three dives. The beacons form a trail, and the trail forms a word nobody can read yet.
Ines finally reads it. It is not a word. It is our crew's own signal pattern, played back.
The deep is listening, and it has been learning from us since the first dive.
A great dark shape below, bigger than the Lanternfish, unmoving, glowing in time with the pulse.
We sent a sonar ping. The shape answered with one of its own. A greeting, or a test.
The last beacons ring the shape like a crown. Every sonar must win its trick now.
Final approach. Every crew mate has a job, and every job comes in order.
The Source falls silent, then answers in our pattern. Contact made. The Lanternfish crew goes home as legends.
